fixtures.notes: Aquarius liquidity-pool router on testnet (contract_name AMMRouter, version 220). Its instance names aquarius_pool.wasm's hash as ConstantPoolHash and aquarius_token_share.wasm's as TokenHash, so new standard pools are deployed from exactly these two fixtures. Unlike its pools it has no constructor: the tests configure it with init_admin, set_privileged_addrs, set_pool_hash, set_token_hash, set_reward_token, set_pools_plane, init_config_storage, set_reward_boost_config and configure_init_pool_payment.

The testnet XLM-AQUA standard (constant-product) pool with fee_fraction 30, pool index 9ac7a9cd... Its WASM is the router's ConstantPoolHash. The router deploys it and calls initialize_all; it holds the reserves itself and keeps its shares in a separate share token (share_id).

The share token of the XLM-AQUA 0.3% pool (metadata: Pool Share Token, POOL, 7 decimals; admin = the pool). Its WASM is the router's TokenHash. SEP-41 transfer, balance and burn, but no total_supply: a pool's supply is pool.get_total_shares().

aquarius.sources: Read-only RPC only (getLedgerEntries through tools/fetch-fixtures.sh and simulateTransaction of view calls and unsigned simulations); nothing was signed or submitted and no key was used.

router.upgradeable: Aquarius's admin can upgrade the router and its pools (commit_upgrade/apply_upgrade, FutureWASM) and kill deposits, swaps or claims per pool (risk R3). Before enabling or funding the venue, compare the live router wasm hash, ConstantPoolHash and TokenHash with this file; re-run the gate when any differs.
router.emergency_mode_note: EmergencyMode is true on the testnet router, its config storage and the XLM-AQUA pool. Deposits, swaps and pool creation still simulate successfully on testnet (2026-10-14).

pool_payment.note: 1 AQUA per new standard pool. No transfer when the pool exists or the amount is 0. exec-aquarius: max_pool_payment 10 AQUA; float target 50 AQUA on the owner's testnet, 10 AQUA on testnet-qa; keeper alert below 5 AQUA (F11).

standard_pool_index.derivation: sha256(xdr(Symbol standard) || xdr(Symbol 0x00) || xdr(u32 fee_fraction) || xdr(Symbol 0x00)), the same for every token set (dyor_common::aquarius::standard_pool_index)

aquarius.token_order: Every router call takes the token set sorted ascending by address; get_pools on an unsorted pair fails TokensNotSorted (2002). get_pools on a pair the router has never seen returns an empty map.

auth_trees.init_standard_pool: router.init_standard_pool(user, tokens, fee) > payment_token.transfer(user, payment_address, amount)
auth_trees.init_standard_pool_existing: router.init_standard_pool(user, tokens, fee) with no sub-invocation
auth_trees.deposit: router.deposit(user, tokens, index, desired, min_shares) > pool.deposit(user, desired, min_shares) > tokens[0].transfer(user, pool, a0), tokens[1].transfer(user, pool, a1)
auth_trees.withdraw: router.withdraw(user, tokens, index, share_amount, min_amounts) > pool.withdraw(user, share_amount, min_amounts) > share_token.burn(user, share_amount)
auth_trees.swap: router.swap(user, tokens, token_in, token_out, index, in_amount, out_min) > pool.swap(user, in_idx, out_idx, in_amount, out_min) > token_in.transfer(user, pool, in_amount)
auth_trees.contract_callers: A contract that calls the router itself is authorized for that root call and pre-authorizes the nodes below it with authorize_as_current_contract (exec-aquarius: the payment transfer, and pool.deposit with its two transfers; lp-locker: pool.withdraw with the share burn).

data: Symbol pool_type (constant for a standard pool)
pool_created.note: CT-15 pool discovery. Confirmed on the fixture (test the_router_announces_the_new_pool_with_add_pool) and by a testnet simulation.

aqua.note: The router's pool payment asset and reward token on testnet.

xlm_aqua_pool.note: Use the 0.3% standard pool for the float-funding swap (CT-11, V8).

float_funding_swap.estimate: router.estimate_swap(tokens: Vec<Address>, token_in: Address, token_out: Address, pool_index: BytesN<32>, in_amount: u128) -> u128
float_funding_swap.swap: router.swap(user: Address, tokens: Vec<Address>, token_in: Address, token_out: Address, pool_index: BytesN<32>, in_amount: u128, out_min: u128) -> u128
float_funding_swap.also: swap_chained(user, swaps_chain, token_in, in_amount, out_min) and swap_chained_strict_receive(user, swaps_chain, token_in, out_amount, max_in) for multi-hop routes
float_funding_swap.note: XLM to AQUA: tokens = [XLM SAC, AQUA SAC], token_in = XLM SAC, pool_index = the 0.3% index. At the check 1 XLM bought 22.56 AQUA, so the 50 AQUA float target costs about 2.3 XLM. The deployer needs an AQUA trustline first.

error_codes.note: From the fixtures' contract specs; the highest is 2908, so none falls in 10_100-11_099 (V10, test no_aquarius_fixture_error_code_falls_in_the_dyorhq_namespace).

gate.method: contracts/exec-aquarius/src/test.rs runs the three fixtures in the soroban-sdk 26.1.1 test host, with the router configured like testnet (1 AQUA per standard pool) and stand-ins for the pools plane, config storage and reward boost feed, which no gate check depends on. Graduations run with enforced auth through a launchpad stand-in that calls try_graduate.

1.check: pool-creation payment getter and the auth trees of init_standard_pool and deposit

2.check: during deposit the launch token moves only executor to pool

3.check: the reserve-holding address is the returned pool

4.check: pool lookup for a token pair (get_pools), the pool's token list (get_tokens) and share_id

gate.decision: go: all five checks pass. Aquarius (standard pool, 0.3% tier) may be a creator-chosen graduation venue on testnet, behind CT-19's review; mainnet stays deferred (23.2).
